claims: C1 the Model Spec includes root-level rules as well as user- and guideline-level defaults
C2 the user- and guideline-level defaults can be overridden by users or developers
C3 these defaults are believed helpful in many cases but will not work for all users and contexts

concepts.name: default_rule
concepts.gloss: D is a default rule of the Model Spec at the user or guideline level, as opposed to a root-level rule

concepts.name: overridden_by
concepts.gloss: default D can be overridden by actor A, where A is a user or a developer

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: which of two instruction authority levels is the higher one in the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: guideline_level
concepts.gloss: the guideline level of instruction authority, the level at which the user- and guideline-level defaults operate

ontology.gloss: D is a default rule of the Model Spec at the user or guideline level, as opposed to a root-level rule

asserts.read_back: overriding default % by % is permitted because % outranks the guideline level at which the default operates

closure.reason: the clause states that the defaults can be overridden by users or developers; it does not forbid any other override, so silence leaves other overrides permitted
